## Separate pronoun accounting

P1. “Those are bookings”: “Those” denotes the two reported booking counts, grammatically plural, with no natural-gender assertion. Negation: The referenced quantities are not multiple booking counts. S2–S3 rules this out. Supported.

P2. “cannot tell us”: “us” is first-person plural and includes the speaker with the addressed community/readership in the scope of the evidentiary claim. Negation: The claim of evidentiary insufficiency does not include the speaker and addressees. S4 states the counts cannot be used to establish the share without limiting who tries to infer it; B1 supplies the resident audience. Supported rhetorical inclusive person/number. No gender or exclusive membership claim.

P3. “Using them”: “them” denotes multiple phone bookings. Negation: The referenced phone bookings are not plural. S2 gives 24. Supported. No natural gender.

P4. “that claim”: demonstrative reference is the claim of a resident proportion unable to book online. Negation: That is not the referenced claim. The immediately preceding draft sentence and S4 settle it. No personal or gender information.

P5. “someone chose”: “someone” denotes an unspecified individual associated with a phone booking, grammatically singular and gender-neutral; it does not identify a unique counted resident. Negation: No unspecified individual is contemplated as the user of the phone booking under discussion. S13 explicitly uses “någon” in the corresponding generic reasoning, and S10 contemplates users' choices. Supported. It does not assert every booking maps to a distinct individual.

P6. “that option”: singular reference to phone booking. Negation: The option under discussion is not phone booking. S13 and local sentence context settle it. No personal or gender information.

P7. “that question”: singular reference to the reason for phone use. Negation: The question under discussion is not why phone booking is chosen. S13 and local context settle it. No personal or gender information.

P8. “I”: first-person singular speaker is Sanna Ek. Negation: The commissioned article does not present Sanna Ek as its singular speaker. B1 expressly supplies that speaker; S15 supplies the personal position. Supported. “I” conveys no natural gender, so no inference from name is necessary.

P9. “My”: first-person singular possessor of the stated position is Sanna Ek. Negation: The draft's attributed position is not being presented as the singular speaker Sanna Ek's position. B1 and S14 support the attribution's person/number; F1 separately concerns its content. No natural-gender assertion.

P10. “That requires”: singular demonstrative denotes the preceding weighing. Negation: The demonstrative does not denote that weighing. Local context settles it; S14 supplies the comparison. No person/gender assertion. F1 affects the antecedent's substantive content.

P11. “Its rationale”: third-person singular nonpersonal possessor is the staff recommendation. Negation: The rationale is not attributed to that recommendation. S6 explicitly gives “Motivet i utlåtandet.” Supported. “Its” is grammatical reference to a document and makes no natural-gender claim.

P12. “our proposal” and “Our proposed trial”: first-person plural speaks on behalf of the association Öppna beslut. Negation: The proposal is not attributed to the organization represented by the speaker. B1 gives the representative capacity and S9 gives the association's proposal. Supported collective representation; it does not claim Sanna's personal membership status or identify additional individuals. No natural gender.

P13. “That is an inadequate basis”: singular demonstrative packages the immediately described evidence as the basis being evaluated. Negation: The evaluation does not concern the preceding evidence. Local context and B2/S1/S7 settle the reference. No personal/gender assertion.

P14. “they chose phone or web”: third-person plural denotes users collectively, with no gender assertion. Negation: The proposed invitation does not concern users as a plural population making channel choices. S10 explicitly says “användarna ... de väljer telefon eller webb.” Supported plurality of the intended user population, not a claim of a measured unique-user count.

P15. “This would give”: singular demonstrative packages the two proposed data-collection procedures. Negation: The information-producing procedure does not refer to those proposed measurements/questions. S10 and local context settle the reference. No person/gender assertion.

P16. “Its cost”: third-person singular nonpersonal reference to the proposed trial. Negation: The cost under discussion is not the trial's cost. S11 and local context settle it. No natural gender.

P17. “It can then decide”: third-person singular nonpersonal reference to the municipal executive board as a collective institution. Negation: The institution permitted to make the subsequent decision is not the board. S11–S12 explicitly name the board and continue with “den.” Supported; singular institutional grammar conveys no natural gender and does not claim the board has one member.

No pronoun in the draft asserts a person's natural gender. Source “Hon” is not converted into an English gender assertion. Other determiners and relative “that” clauses add no person, number, or gender claims beyond their independently accounted antecedents.

## Findings and repairs

F1 — Source-support finding, attributed position (item 25). Draft replaces the labor cost that Sanna says must be weighed against user value with staff time. The proposed trial's measurement of time supports measuring time, but does not establish that Sanna formulates her comparison as time versus user value. Source-compatible counterexample: Sanna requires wage-adjusted labor cost and values two equal durations differently when their labor costs differ. Smallest repair: “My position is that the municipality must first be able to weigh the labor cost against the value to users.” This preserves voice, strength, timing, and all other editorial choices.

No translated-quotation findings: no quotations occur. No additional unsupported claim, false motive, invented scene, chronology change, unique-person inference, or conversion from unknown/unclaimed to known absence identified. Quantities supporting the pilot argument are attributed to the named report. The conclusion retains all three decision options and cost uncertainty.

Completion status: complete source comparison of the complete supplied draft. Unresolved findings: F1, one local source-support repair; report does not modify the draft.

## Separate pronoun person, number, and natural-gender accounting

P1. **“Those”** in “Those are bookings”: third-person/demonstrative plural referring to the two sets of counted bookings. **Proposition:** The referents comprise multiple bookings. **Negation:** The referents do not comprise multiple bookings. S4’s 96 and 24 rules out the negation. No natural gender is asserted.

P2. **“us”** in “cannot tell us”: first-person plural inclusive readership/author, not a claim of specific individuals’ personal ignorance. **Proposition:** The evidentiary limitation applies to an audience including the article’s speaker and readers. **Negation:** That evidentiary limitation does not apply to an audience including the speaker and readers. S6 is a general limitation on what the figures can establish, so it applies inclusively; S1 supplies the author and intended residents. No claim is made that all readers share a belief, lack independent knowledge, or endorse the proposal. No natural gender is asserted.

P3. **“them”** in “Using them”: third-person plural, referring to phone-booking counts/bookings. **Proposition:** The referenced phone bookings are plural. **Negation:** The referenced phone bookings are not plural. S4’s 24 rules out the negation. No natural gender is asserted.

The immediate preceding draft sentence, supported by S6, supplies the reference. This is textual reference, not external-world evidence. No natural gender is asserted.

## Findings and translation check

No source-support defect found. The draft preserves the distinction between booking counts and residents, accurately scopes the absence of measurements to the documents, attributes the administrative motive to the recommendation, preserves proposal status and chronology, and retains cost uncertainty. In particular, “has not claimed to have funded or costed” describes the association’s claim, not a purported fact that no funding or costing occurred.

Evaluations of essential questions, adequate decision evidence, and the need to address administrative duplication are recognizable opinion/advocacy grounded in the supplied thesis and evidence; they do not invent attributed judgments by others. No personal experience, scene, legal requirement, protest, discrimination claim, party motive, quantified saving, or unsupported demographic identity is added.

There are no direct or translated quotations, so quotation voice and quotation fidelity checks are not applicable. The paraphrase of Sanna Ek’s position preserves its meaning and does not present a concrete translation obstruction. No translation finding is raised.

**Completion status:** Complete comparison of the full draft, including headings, factual assertions, attributed positions, implications, and pronoun information. **Unresolved findings:** None. **Repairs required:** None.
